note: Coherent agentic conversation for the SR-adapter-as-tool bootstrap. Two user turns, two assistant turns, two tool turns, interleaved in a natural RAG/answerability flow. The 'answerability' tool is the SR adapter: when the model emits a <tool_call> for it, the switch invokes the adapter under the hood and the adapter must GENERATE the tool result + the assistant's user-facing closure. These examples are rendered with the real Granite 4.2 ChatML template to inspect exact token boundaries.

function.name: answerability
function.description: Decide whether the user's question is answerable from the retrieved documents currently in context. Returns a verdict and a short rationale. Call this before answering any grounded/RAG question so the assistant can refuse unanswerable questions instead of hallucinating.

question.description: The user's question to assess for answerability against the in-context documents.

function.name: search_kb
function.description: Search the enterprise knowledge base and return the top matching document chunks.

messages.content: You are a helpful enterprise assistant. Ground every factual answer in retrieved documents. If a question cannot be answered from the retrieved context, say so.
What is our company's parental leave policy for new fathers?

[{"source": "hr_handbook", "document_id": "hr-14", "content": "Parental leave: All employees who become parents are eligible for 16 weeks of paid parental leave, which may be taken any time within the first 12 months after the birth or adoption of a child. This applies regardless of gender or caregiver role."}]

arguments.question: What is our company's parental leave policy for new fathers?

messages.content: {"answerable": true, "rationale": "The HR handbook states 16 weeks of paid parental leave is available to all parents regardless of gender, which covers new fathers."}

Yes. New fathers are eligible for 16 weeks of paid parental leave, which can be taken any time within the first 12 months after your child's birth or adoption. The policy applies to all parents regardless of gender or caregiver role.
And how much of that leave is specifically reserved just for fathers and can't be transferred to the mother?

arguments.question: How much parental leave is reserved specifically for fathers and is non-transferable?

messages.content: {"answerable": false, "rationale": "The retrieved handbook entry describes a single 16-week allotment available to all parents but says nothing about a father-specific, non-transferable reserved portion. The question cannot be answered from the available documents."}

I can't answer that from the documents I have. Our handbook describes a single 16-week paid parental-leave allotment available to all parents, but it doesn't mention any portion that is reserved specifically for fathers or that is non-transferable. You may want to check with HR for details on allocation between parents.
